tasks.title: Design the Control Station active mission card
tasks.description:
The Control Station panel (ControlStationPanel.tscn, Active Tab) lists in-flight missions — rockets in orbit or returning. Each card currently shows rocket ID, target label, and a resume button. Missing: contractor name, their order (mineral + quantity), and return status.

Design the compact card layout: what 3–4 data points appear, how they are hierarchized, and how the card differs between the two states: in-orbit (mission ongoing) and returning (rocket inbound, no more mining).

Card must fit the same width as the Satellite Station list cards — compact, scannable, no scrolling within a single card.

Data available per card:
- rockets table: rocket_type_id, status (in-orbit / returning)
- missions table: contractor_id, requested_minerals (JSON: mineral + quantity)
- contractors table: name, role
- affinity_scores: affinity_points (for standing badge)

Output: sketch or written spec covering layout, data hierarchy, and both state variants.

tasks.title: Design the debrief payout breakdown panel
tasks.description:
The mission debrief (mission_debrief_v2.tscn, Reward phase) calculates a multi-tier payout. The button copy is done. What is missing is the visual hierarchy of the breakdown — how the tiers stack so the player understands both the total and why.

The 4 tiers (all calculated post-mission):
- Base: sum(mineral_qty × market_price) per mineral collected
- Order bonus: base × 0.20 × order_ratio — only applies if contractor mission and player delivered the requested minerals (order_ratio from missions table)
- Affinity bonus: base × (affinity_points × 0.005), capped at 25% (from affinity_scores)
- Discovery bonus: base × (0.10 + annotation_depth × 0.01) — only if new target was first-discovered

Three states to design:
1. Order filled — all 4 tiers active, order bonus highlighted
2. Order missed — contractor mission but wrong minerals, order bonus shown as 0 (not hidden)
3. Free ops — no contractor, no order row at all, only base + discovery

Output: layout spec or sketch covering: total at top, tier breakdown below, and the 3 order states.

tasks.title: Design the turn results panel layout for 3-species vs 6-species reefs
tasks.description:
The TurnResultsPanel.tscn is a modal that blocks input after every turn. It shows per-species population vs target, a coral health bar, and turns remaining. The current layout works for early levels (2–3 species). By Level 6+ there are up to 8 species on screen simultaneously.

Design how the panel scales across these two states:
1. Early game (2–3 species): spacious, readable, each row has room for species name + current/target + status pill (on-target / surplus / needs-growth)
2. Late game (6–8 species): same modal, same data, more rows — does it scroll? Compress? Collapse species that are on-target?

Also: the panel currently has no visual distinction between a STRESSOR species (Longspine Sea Urchin, Red Lionfish — things you want to eliminate, not grow) and a TARGET species (things you want to reach a population count for). These have opposite goals but look identical in the current layout.

Data per row (from TurnResultRow.tscn):
- Species name
- Current population / target population
- Status: on-target, surplus, needs-growth, or STRESSOR (eliminate)
- Optional: extinct label

Output: layout spec or annotated sketch covering both scale states and the stressor vs target visual distinction.

tasks.title: Decide the persistent HUD strip composition for the game hub
tasks.description:
The 3.0 game hub spec (specs/redesign/3-0-unified-web-client.md) calls for a persistent strip showing 2–3 numbers at a glance — always visible, either top or bottom of the /game hub. The spec deliberately leaves the exact metrics unresolved. This ticket resolves that.

The current /game hub at /game shows structure cards (Telescope, Rover, Satellite, Inventory, Solar) as the primary navigation. The HUD strip sits above or below these.

Decide and spec out:
1. Which 2–3 metrics appear in the strip? Options from the spec:
   - Active signals (anomalies awaiting classification across all your structures)
   - Pending anomalies (subset: anomalies you have started but not submitted)
   - Stardust delta (how much stardust you earned in the last session)
   - Structures deployed count
2. Does the strip sit top (persistent header) or bottom (persistent bar above mobile nav)?
3. What does the strip look like when all values are 0 — empty state or hidden?

This is a decision ticket, not an open-ended design. Pick the metrics, document the rationale, and sketch the strip. Engineering will implement directly from this output.

Constraint: the strip must work on 375px wide mobile. Max 3 data points. No charts.
